source.postgres: PostgreSQL 16.2 on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (GCC) 10.2.1 20210130 (Red Hat 10.2.1-11), 64-bit

theoretical_volume.note: The latter assumes client batching at the 4 Hz request rate; neither is a server-enforced rate ceiling.

retention.behavior: Journal rows are append-only and retained with wave history; no automatic cleanup or retention cap was found in the current migrations.

limits: Timing is in-process against disposable local Unix-socket PostgreSQL and excludes internet/network latency.
Allocated relation/index sizes are scratch-database-wide PostgreSQL relation sizes, not isolated per-wave index attribution.
The 10k bounded workload is a diagnostic sample, not a production-capacity guarantee.
No server request-rate limiter exists, so the 4 Hz input model is representative client behavior rather than a hard upper bound.
